summary: The issue body's mutation figures were stale by construction: rogue3#57 claims 7 of 23 single-edit mutants survive SelfTest, but re-deriving the inventory against current main (48b3a6a, after rogue3#46 rewrote the area) measured 17 of 24 surviving. Every number in the issue predated the merge it depends on.
evidence: issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#57;command:dotnet fsi build.fsx -t SelfTest (111 case(s), 0 failure(s) at 48b3a6a, vs the 30 and 77 case counts quoted in the issue and its comment)
cost: Full re-derivation of the mutant inventory before any code could be written; roughly one third of the cycle.
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 - issue authoring; any hardening issue that quotes a mutation sweep should pin the commit the sweep ran on and be re-derived by the implementer.

summary: A one-edit-per-tree mutation sweep over git archive exports is cheap enough to run as an ordinary development loop here, because the target under test is BCL-only and needs no restore: SelfTest runs in 1.8s, so a 39-mutant sweep costs about two minutes and can be re-run after every change to the fix.
evidence: command:git archive HEAD | tar -x -C <tmp> then dotnet fsi build.fsx -t SelfTest per mutated tree;command:time ./fake.sh build -t SelfTest (real 0m1.805s before the fix, 0m3.549s after, the doubling being the child self-probe)
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 - build.fsx SelfTest; the hermetic BCL-only constraint recorded in .github/workflows/verify.yml is what makes this affordable and is worth preserving deliberately.

summary: A mutation harness that scores survival on exit code alone silently miscounts F# COMPILE ERRORS as killed mutants. Three of my mutants (two vacuous-check forms and one probe-removal) did not compile, exited 1, and were scored killed; the vacuous-check row is load-bearing because four combination mutants were built on top of it and were therefore also void.
evidence: command:dotnet fsi build.fsx -t SelfTest on a mutated export emitting 'build.fsx(1153,57): error FS0072', scored exit=1 killed with 0 ok lines and no summary line
cost: Two re-runs of the affected sweep rows and one silently wrong intermediate inventory that would have been reported as fact.
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 - any future mutation sweep; the fix is to require a mutant to still produce the harness's summary line, or to compile-check the tree separately, before scoring it.

summary: Any edit to build.fsx forces an append to scripts/audit-binding-exceptions.json, which is the one file two concurrent workers were already contending over. The audit-binding gate binds build.fsx by digest from at least four merged audits, so a hardening item whose entire declared path is build.fsx cannot avoid the contended file.
evidence: command:python3 scripts/check-audit-bindings.py (exit 1, naming file:build.fsx stale in feedback/audits/2026-08-02-Rogue3-{4,7,15}.audit.json and 2026-08-02-Rogue3.audit.json);issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#53
cost: One overlap declaration, one coordination message to the concurrent worker, and the ledger append deferred to the last edit before the PR.
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 - scripts/check-audit-bindings.py and the audit-binding ledger design; a per-worker ledger or an append-only format with no whole-file digest would remove the contention.

summary: The Verify target is red on main for a reason unrelated to any item under work, and CI never runs it, so every worker must independently rediscover that the red is inherited rather than theirs. PerformanceEvidence rejects route digests declared in EvidenceCommands.fs after PR #59 changed Model.fs without re-declaring them.
evidence: command:./fake.sh build -t Verify (exit 1, 'status=failed m7-ui-performance routes=4' then 'PerformanceEvidence failed with exit code 1', while TemplateDrift, GeneratedGuidanceCheck and 253/253 tests all passed);issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#61
cost: One full Verify run plus a diff-scope check to prove the failure was inherited and not caused by this change.
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 - readiness/performance evidence declaration in src/Rogue3/EvidenceCommands.fs, and .github/workflows/verify.yml for the fact that CI never exercises Verify.

summary: Two successive CI guards for this gate were defeated by forging the transcript they read, which is a general result rather than two accidents: grepping for FAIL was fail-open to renaming one printf, and its replacement requiring ok-count == case-count was fail-open to one contiguous edit rewriting the failure branch into a success print. A self-checking harness needs a machine-readable result channel from the start.
evidence: command:mutation sweep row D2 at 48b3a6a (vacuous check plus failure-branch rewrite: 111 cases, 111 ok lines, exit 0, both SelfTest and the ok-count guard green);file:.github/workflows/verify.yml
cost: The gate shipped twice with a guard that a single cosmetic edit disarmed.
owner: EHotwagner/fs-gg scaffolding - any generated self-test target should emit a structured result artifact alongside its human transcript, so a CI guard never has to parse stdout.

summary: An audit-binding exception is pinned to ONE observed digest, so appending to the excuse ledger before the source bytes are final silently invalidates the excuse just written. My first --grandfather went stale when two review rounds forced further edits to build.fsx, leaving PR #71 red on a gate that had already been satisfied once.
evidence: command:python3 scripts/check-audit-bindings.py (exit 1 after the ledger had been rewritten once, exit 0 only after re-running --grandfather on the final bytes);file:scripts/audit-binding-exceptions.json;issue:EHotwagner/rogue3#53
cost: One red CI cycle on an otherwise green PR, plus a second --grandfather run; the concurrent worker on rogue3#55 reported hitting the identical trap three times in one cycle.
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 - scripts/check-audit-bindings.py; the remedy text names the pinning behaviour but nothing warns that the append must be the LAST edit, which is the operational rule two workers independently had to learn.

summary: Two critics under deliberately different rubrics found disjoint defect sets on the same green candidate, and neither set would have been found by the other. The mutation critic found an environment variable that silently neutered a defence; the design and honesty critic found a second gate defeat by reading which functions a defence actually covered, without running a single mutant.
evidence: command:TMPDIR=$PWD dotnet fsi build.fsx -t SelfTest on a tree carrying a cwd-keyed exemption and real kit drift (exit 0 before the fix, exit 1 after);file:build.fsx
cost: none - both found before merge; without them two single-edit gate defeats would have shipped inside the change that claimed to close gate defeats.
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 - worker orchestration policy; requiring critics to carry DIFFERENT rubrics rather than running two mutation sweeps is what produced the disjointness.

summary: Path.GetTempPath() honours $TMPDIR, so any hardening that relies on standing somewhere other than the repository is silently defeatable from the environment. A defence that relocated the process to Path.GetTempPath() became a no-op under TMPDIR set to the repository root, turning a killed mutant back into a green gate with real kit drift on disk.
evidence: command:TMPDIR=$PWD dotnet fsi build.fsx -t SelfTest on an export carrying a cwd-keyed exemption plus planted kit drift (exit 0 before the fix, exit 1 after);file:build.fsx
cost: One blocking review round; the defence had already shipped in the PR and read as correct.
owner: EHotwagner/rogue3 - build.fsx; generalises to any FS.GG scaffold code that treats the system temp directory as a location outside the workspace.
